target_customer: Life sciences companies, payers and providers that need data on doctors and healthcare organizations
problem: Information about healthcare professionals is fragmented, so pharma and others struggle to find the right doctor for trials, outreach and network building.
product_category: Healthcare professional and organization data platform

founders.name: Ariel Katz
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page, Wikipedia and TechCrunch.

founders.name: Ian Sax
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page and Wikipedia.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a database of over 8 million professional profiles (TechCrunch Apr 2020) means large scale data ingestion and entity matching, solid but standard data engineering.

defensibility.rationale: The accumulated profile database and pharma customer relationships were hard to rebuild quickly, though underlying sources such as public records are available to rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent buying or copying H1 was found. H1 itself became an acquirer (Carevoyance 2021, Ribbon Health, Veda Data Solutions, Defacto Health).

market_need_then: Life sciences and payers wanted to identify clinicians for trials and outreach. By April 2020 H1 had more than 8 million profiles and revenue, and investors funded a $12.9M Series A within months of YC.

branding.name_origin: Katz says H1 refers to the statistical representation of a true hypothesis, as opposed to the null hypothesis H0 (Wikipedia).
branding.domain_note: Originally h1.co, now h1.com (h1.co redirects with a 301). Company was formerly H1 Insights.

rebrands.why: Not stated; a USPTO record shows an H1 trademark filed November 2021 by H1 Insights, Inc. and a homepage banner mentions a new look.

brand_strength.rationale: Clean short name with a meaningful story and large pharma customer base, but H1 collides with the US visa name and no community or brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: H1 sold data on healthcare professionals to life sciences firms, raised $12.9M Series A in April 2020 and a $58M Series B in December 2020, then a $100M Series C in November 2021 with a 2022 extension, and grew to about 500 staff. Its proprietary database and pharma sales motion drove rapid funding, and it later made several acquisitions. It is active with no exit.
notes: The 2018 $6M Shore Group amount comes from Wikipedia only and the stage is not labeled by it. The Menlo lead of the Series A rests on TechCrunch Dec 2020 stating Menlo led the earlier financing. A $773M valuation after the 2022 extension and a 2026 $40M round led by CVS Health Ventures appear in single secondary sources and are not recorded. Competitor list is empty: Crunchbase reportedly lists Komodo Health and Definitive Healthcare as rivals but no source dated near 2020 was found. Wikipedia lists acquisitions and 2026 events. A Blind thread mentions layoffs, unconfirmed.
